# NeuralSheet

> Audio-to-MIDI transcription as a native macOS app. Record or drop a track, pick the instruments, and NeuralSheet turns it into MIDI you can play back, mix, edit and drag into your DAW. Transcription runs entirely on the Mac; nothing is uploaded.

NeuralSheet is a free, open-source (Apache-2.0) app by Quassum for macOS 26 and later on Apple silicon. It is a from-scratch Swift rewrite of NeuralNote by Damien Ronssin and uses the MuScriptor transcription model (Kyutai and Mirelo) through muscriptor.cpp on Metal.

## Key facts

- Platform: macOS 26 or later, Apple silicon only. Signed and notarized disk image.
- Price: free. Code under Apache-2.0; the model weights are CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial) and are downloaded separately on first run.
- Input: recording from any audio device, or .wav, .aiff, .flac, .mp3 and .ogg files.
- Output: multi-track .mid files (one track per instrument, drums on channel 10) or drag-and-drop of MIDI into a DAW.
- Models: small (209 MB), medium (618 MB, recommended), large (2.7 GB); about 3.5x, 1.5x and 0.5x real time on an M1 Pro.
- Editing: move, resize, draw, erase, reassign instrument, velocity, snap and quantize to a tempo grid, undo.
- Playback: the built-in General MIDI synthesizer, mixed against the original audio, with per-instrument level, mute and solo.
- Updates: new versions are published automatically on GitHub Releases.
